items_missed: Never asked the customer's name and never used it once in the entire call
Never asked 'How are you today?' after the greeting
No agenda statement (what the call would cover, ~10-15 min) and no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation

Didn't ask for address/zip, additional rooms, special considerations (hallways/turns), packing needs, box count, storage, additional stops, or access concerns — only home size and stairs surfaced because the customer volunteered them unprompted

No 'pricing is super simple' opener, no explanation of what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, tools) beyond mentioning moving blankets/shrink wrap, and no disassembly/reassembly mention despite the customer describing two beds still assembled with frames
No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and the 'no hidden fees' pitch were all never mentioned
Clock explanation only covered the 2.5-hour minimum — never explained that the clock starts on-site or the 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum, and no 'does that make sense?' sense-check

The entire Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped — no consolidation tips, no 'take a carload' tip, no shorter-move-lower-bill framing — despite this being a job with dressers, a cabinet, and loose items that would clearly benefit from prep
No deposit-not-required statement, no email/confirmation handoff offered at all, and no 'any other questions before I let you go?' or branch hours/contact info given before ending the call
Never attempted a firm close — let the customer end the call with 'I'll call back' without reinforcing the two open slots (afternoon 7/31, afternoon 8/1) or asking for a verbal lock-in
top_strength: Hector handled a chaotic, interruption-heavy call (background noise, a crying child, the customer stepping away mid-sentence) with patience and clear pricing math, walking through the $107/mover hourly rate, the $214 two-mover rate, the 2.5-hour minimum, and the free-travel-zone check for Frisco without ever losing his composure or rushing the customer.
coaching_note: Hector delivered pricing and the estimate range well but skipped nearly every differentiator (No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) and the full Save Your Ass speech — build a simple pre-call checklist so those four items get said on every call regardless of how the conversation flows, since right now they're being dropped entirely rather than just softened.
phone_presence_notes: Hector stayed warm and patient through repeated interruptions ('Oh, you're fine sir, it's okay, it's all good' and 'Appreciate your patience with me, I know you got a little one over there needing some help'), and the customer ended the call clearly satisfied ('Perfect, thank you so much'), though Hector never once used the customer's name.
